Enough to take pictures from outside
Oct 2026 • Friends
The Café Apartment at 42 Nguyễn Huệ in Ho Chi Minh City is a nine-story building once a residence, now transformed into a lively complex of independent cafés, boutiques, and eateries. Its eclectic, bustling atmosphere is filled with vintage shops, craft stores, and small coffee spots, each showcasing unique styles and neon signs adorning balconies and windows. Visitors can take the free stairs or pay a small elevator fee, which is refundable when they purchase at participating shops.

This spot is especially photogenic at night, when the lights illuminate the balconies and create a picturesque scene. However, the worn stairwells and some potentially gimmicky or overpriced cafes might come off as just another tourist trap. Taking photos outside along Nguyen Hue Walking Street is enough to capture its charm, rather than venturing inside to explore every floor.

Not sure
Jan 2026 • Couples
The place is nice, but nothing special. It’s not really worth making a detour to visit or going out of your way for it. It’s a big building with several cafés inside, and none of the cafés really stand out—they all serve the same kind of basic things. It’s more about saying you’ve been there, in that building where all the old apartments have apparently been replaced by individual cafés. None of them are exceptionally good or bad; it’s just standard fare.

It might be worth taking a photo from the outside, because it’s kind of nice to see each old apartment balcony turned into a different café terrace, so it creates a kind of patchwork effect. But beyond that, climbing the stairs and trying all the cafés isn’t really something I’d say is worth it. There are far more interesting things to do in Saigon—like visiting the War Museum, taking photos of the opera house or the theater, or just enjoying the really nice individual street cafés that are actually worth it. Here, you’re kind of crammed into a big shoebox of little boxes, and it just lacks space, air, and punch.

The Café Apartment at 42 Nguyễn Huệ in Ho Chi Minh City is a nine-story building once a residence, now transformed into a lively complex of independent cafés, boutiques, and eateries. Its eclectic, bustling atmosphere is filled with vintage shops, craft stores, and small coffee spots, each showcasing unique styles and neon signs adorning balconies and windows. Visitors can take the free stairs or pay a small elevator fee, which is refundable when they purchase at participating shops.

This spot is especially photogenic at night, when the lights illuminate the balconies and create a picturesque scene. However, the worn stairwells and some potentially gimmicky or overpriced cafes might come off as just another tourist trap. Taking photos outside along Nguyen Hue Walking Street is enough to capture its charm, rather than venturing inside to explore every floor.
